title: 1907-1908 — New Year editorial, Savoy Star
text:
1907-1908

So far as the Star is concerned this issue closes the year of 1907. To many this has been a hard year caused by short crops in this section. To many it has brought sadness. Children have gone from the parental roof to make homes of their own, which, in some instances have not been happy. Sickness and affliction have entered the home, and loved ones been taken from the earth to their home eternal. These things cause sadness, but still, we know this is the common fate of man, and there are other things that should cause us to rejoice as we behold the old year pass out.

We are surrounded by good friends who are ever ready to minister to our needs; and, while we may not have all the money we want, none of us will go hungry or cold because of actual poverty. During the past twelve months, we have had unlimited opportunities for doing good, and it is to be hoped we have improved them.

With these things on our minds, let us take courage and start in the new year with greater expectations, greater determinations, and greater aspirations, and success will be inevitable. We hope to see 1908 bring a good crop and put money in the people's pockets, smiles on their faces, and good cheer in their hearts.
notes: Clipping is yellowed and worn; some words partially obscured by fold or damage at middle of page. The heading '1907-1908' indicates this is a year-end editorial. Publication is the Savoy Star.
